title: SDK Degrade Orchestra: Observability-Driven Fallbacks & Cost Shepherding Playbook
author: Asha Kumar
body:
Overview

This playbook documents an opinionated, reproducible approach (the "Degrade Orchestra") for SDK teams integrating Redwood Inference: combining observable signals, automated fallback orchestration, and cost-shepherding policies. It is written for SDK owners, runtime integrators, and developer-platform engineers who need a deterministic way to reduce cost and preserve availability when backend inference quality or capacity is degraded.

Goals
- Define observable signals and thresholds that drive graceful degradation.
- Provide policy templates for automated fallback actions (client-side & server-triggered).
- Ship SDK configuration and code snippets to implement the patterns.
- Provide a step-by-step rollback, testing, and canary checklist.

Audience
- SDK maintainers (all languages)
- Developer experience engineers integrating Redwood APIs
- Support engineers who triage production regressions

Key Concepts
1) Signals (observable inputs): latency percentiles, token cost per request, model-quality score (client-side eval), error ratios, queue depth, and KV cache hit rate.
2) Actions: switch model variant, reduce max_tokens, enable local summarization/abstraction, throttle requests, route to cached-response fabric, or fall back to stateless smaller model.
3) Policies: rule sets mapping Signals -> Actions, prioritized and time-bound.
4) Cost-shepherding: objective function to prefer actions that minimize cost uplift while respecting latency/quality SLOs.

Signal definitions and thresholds (recommended defaults)
- latency_p50_ms: normal < 120ms, warning >= 200ms, critical >= 500ms
- latency_p95_ms: normal < 450ms, warning >= 800ms, critical >= 1500ms
- error_rate_5m: normal < 0.5%, warning >= 1.5%, critical >= 4%
- token_cost_per_minute: normal baseline, warning when +30% vs baseline, critical when +75%
- model_quality_drop_pct: percent drop vs golden prompts, warning >= 5%, critical >= 12%

Telemetry event schema (SDK -> Observability)
The SDK should emit lightweight telemetry events describing degraded-path decisions. Use the following JSON event schema (example):

{
  "event_type": "fallback_decision",
  "timestamp": "2026-12-02T14:21:00Z",
  "request_id": "req_1234abcd",
  "observed_signals": ["latency_p95_ms:820","error_rate_5m:2.3%","kv_cache_hit:12%"],
  "decision": "switch_model_variant",
  "action_params": ["variant:fast-quant","max_tokens:128"],
  "reason": "latency_p95_ms exceeded critical threshold",
  "sdk_version": "v1.4.2",
  "region": "us-west-2"
}

(Emit as a single-line JSON to the platform telemetry endpoint; redact PII.)

Policy templates
- Conservative (default): take single-step actions, prefer cache & small quantized model.
- Aggressive: reduce max_tokens by 50% and switch to tiny model after first warning.
- Cost-first: proactively throttle top-10% high-cost requests, enable prompt-based truncation.

Example YAML policy (Conservative):

policy_name: conserve-availability
priority: 10
triggers:
  - signal: latency_p95_ms
    op: gt
    value: 800
    window: 5m
    severity: critical
actions:
  - type: switch_model_variant
    params: { variant: fast-quant }
  - type: set_request_cap
    params: { max_tokens: 128 }
  - type: emit_telemetry
    params: { level: warning }

SDK integration examples
1) Python (recommended runtime hooks):

from redwood import Client, DegradeOrchestra

client = Client(api_key=os.environ.get('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
orchestra = DegradeOrchestra(client, policy='conserve-availability')

# wrapper that applies orchestration automatically
@orchestra.guard
def generate(prompt, max_tokens=512):
    return client.generate(prompt=prompt, max_tokens=max_tokens)

# local fallback example: if orchestration appears, return a cached short answer
result = generate('Summarize the release notes')

2) TypeScript (browser / edge SDK):

import { RedwoodClient, DegradeOrchestra } from '@redwood/sdk';
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
const orchestra = new DegradeOrchestra(client, { policy: 'cost-first' });

// usage pattern: instrumented call with optional local truncation
await orchestra.call('complete', { prompt, maxTokens: 256 });

Operational runbook (short):
1) Detect: PagerAlert from platform when latency_p95 > 1200ms or error_rate_5m > 3%.
2) Triage: Check telemetry events for "fallback_decision" in the last 15m.
3) If fallback is active and user impact low: observe for 5m.
4) If fallback active and user-facing errors persist: revert policy to less-aggressive or disable orchestration.
5) Roll forward: re-enable conservative policy, raise max_tokens gradually, monitor quality golden set.

Escalation thresholds and contacts
- On-call SRE: paging if critical sustained > 10 minutes.
- SDK owner: page when a fallback decision affects > 5% of production traffic for > 30 minutes.
- Product PM: notify if model_quality_drop_pct > 8% for > 1 hour.

Rollout and testing checklist (pre-merge)
- Unit tests: local decision engine test coverage >= 85%.
- Integration tests: simulated signals (latency/error/cost) drive expected actions.
- Golden prompts: verify quality regressions under fallback policies within 2% delta vs baseline.
- Canary: deploy to 1% of traffic, run for 4 hours, check telemetry events for false positives.
- Observability: dashboards created for fallback decisions, model variant switches, and request-cost distribution.

Dashboards & Alerts to create
- Fallback Decisions Over Time (count by decision type)
- Traffic % under fallback by region and client SDK version
- Mean token_cost_per_request and 95th percentile by route
- Golden prompt quality regression chart (rolling 24h)
- Alert: > 1% traffic under "aggressive" policy for 15m

Sample query (Metrics system)
- count_over_time({ event = "fallback_decision", decision = "switch_model_variant" }[15m]) > 100

Common support patterns / canonical fixes
1) False-positive latency triggers: increase latency threshold by 10% for the affected region and tighten sampling for telemetry.
2) Regressions in quality after switching variant: add an immediate rollback action to the policy and schedule a model-onboarding review.
3) Cost noise from bursty embed requests: add per-tenant token budget with soft-throttling and notify tenant owner.
4) SDK versions not emitting telemetry: rollout compatibility shim and backfill by re-issuing small sampling of calls.

Troubleshooting matrix (quick)
- Symptom: sudden increase in fallback_decision events
  - Check: background load (queue depth), recent deploys, model health API status
  - Fix: scale Dedicated capacity, adjust policy thresholds, or pin model version
- Symptom: client rejections after fallback
  - Check: client SDK compatibility and schema mismatch in action_params
  - Fix: release a small SDK patch that tolerates missing fields; add server-side graceful defaults

Ownership and governance
- SDK Degrade Orchestra owners: eng-developer-experience team (primary), eng-serving-runtime (secondary).
- Policy changes require: RFC + 2 approvers (one from SRE, one from Product).
- Emergency policy overrides can be applied by SRE with post-facto RFC within 48 hours.

Appendix A — Example telemetry event mapping table
- event_name: fallback_decision -> emits metadata + action_params
- event_name: policy_evaluation -> emits matched rules, signal values, and evaluation latency
- event_name: cache_hit -> emits cache_key, ttl_remaining, response_age

Appendix B — Quick sample: CLI for local testing
# simulate high latency and observe policy output
redwood-cli simulate-signals --latency_p95_ms 1200 --error_rate_5m 2.0 --policy conserve-availability --output events.log

Appendix C — References and related pages
- SDK telemetry schema (internal): /confluence/eng-developer-experience/docs-site/sdk-telemetry-schema-2025
- Model onboarding quality checklist: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/model-onboarding/quality-goldens-2026

Notes and guidance
- Keep actions as idempotent and fast as possible; SDK should not block main thread for policy evaluation.
- Avoid hard-coded tenant-level thresholds; use per-tenant baseline computed from 24h historical metrics.
- Respect privacy: do not emit prompt text in telemetry. Emit hashes if necessary.

If you are implementing this pattern and need pairing help, open a PR and tag eng-developer-experience.
